To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
partial saturation, lower void ratios, and rest load higher than 400N are remedies for fictive negative pore pressures in biphasc finite element models during unloading.
the computation of negative pressure upon unloading can be prevented by: (a) defining a partial saturated model, (b) using a lower VR or (c) using a boundary pressure and a rest load.
the use of an RL higher than 400N, the use of a partial saturated disc model or a lower VR, or a combination of all three, can be used to avoid fictive negative pressures.

the development of a biphasic finite-element model that predicts realistic disc pressures upon unloading.
the development of a finite element model of the intervertebraldisc that is able to simulate the unloading phase.
the development of constitutive relations that can predict the mechanical behavior of the disc during loading and unloading.

a partial saturation of the disc and/or the use of an adequate VR in the disc tissue are the remedies to avoid fictive negative pressure in finite element models.
a partial saturation, a lower VR, and an RL of 350-400 N should be considered when modeling unloading of a spinal segment.
